alt: Sold as the TLX from the 2015 model year; TLX problems are listed under 2015 and later

issues.t: Front lower ball joints can wear out and separate
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from the front over bumps, loose or vague steering, and uneven front tire wear.
issues.why: Some cars of this generation were built with front lower ball joints that wear out too early. A badly worn joint can pull apart and let the front suspension drop.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 99V-069 and have the free ball joint replacement done. If the front end clunks or the steering feels loose, have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Transmission case bolt can fall out
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive while moving, or the car rolling while in Park.
issues.why: A bolt in the transmission case can work loose and fall out, letting the transmission separate from the differential. When that happens the car loses drive and Park no longer holds it.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 99V-227 and have the redesigned bolt installed. Always set the parking brake until it is done.

issues.t: Automatic transmission wear and failure
issues.sym: Slipping, flaring revs between gears, slow or harsh shifts, or a flashing D or D4 light on the dash.
issues.why: The five-speed automatic in this generation is known to wear out early inside, and Honda extended warranty coverage on many of these units at the time. That coverage has since run out.
issues.next: Change the fluid regularly with genuine Honda fluid and get slipping or a flashing D light diagnosed right away. A failed unit usually needs a rebuild or replacement.

issues.t: Second gear can overheat and break
issues.sym: Grinding or clunking from the transmission, harsh shifting, or the transmission locking up while driving.
issues.why: Too little oil reached the second gear set, so the gears could overheat, chip and break. A broken gear can lock the transmission.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 04V-176. Dealers revise the cooler line and replace the transmission if overheat damage is found. Stop driving if the transmission grinds or locks up.

issues.t: Driver air bag inflator can rupture
issues.sym: No warning signs. The defect only shows up if the driver air bag goes off in a crash.
issues.why: The original driver air bag inflator (not a Takata part) can rupture or underinflate the bag when it deploys. Some later replacement modules with the same inflator type were also recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls 20V-026 and 20V-027 and get the free repair right away.

issues.t: High-risk driver air bag inflator (do not drive)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The danger only appears if the driver air bag deploys.
issues.why: These TLs used a high-risk Takata driver inflator that can explode and throw metal fragments. Honda has told owners with unrepaired cars to stop driving them.
issues.next: Do not drive the car until recall 15V-320 is done. Check the VIN and have the car towed to an Acura dealer for the free repair.

issues.t: Power steering hose can crack and leak onto the exhaust
issues.sym: Power steering fluid drips, a whining pump, heavier steering, or smoke and a burning smell from under the hood.
issues.why: Long exposure to engine heat makes the power steering hose break down and crack. Fluid that leaks onto the hot catalytic converter can smoke or start a fire.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls 08V-091 and 12V-222 and get the heat-resistant hose installed. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Windshield wipers stop working
issues.sym: Wipers that work only sometimes, stop mid-sweep, or quit completely, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get into the wiper motor through a vent, corrode it and trip the motor's internal circuit breaker.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 08V-092 and have the motor replaced. Do not drive in rain or snow without working wipers.

issues.t: Engine can stall from a failing fuel pump relay
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving without warning, or the car cranks but will not start.
issues.why: A fault in the fuel pump relay can cut power to the fuel pump, which starves the engine of fuel.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for open recall 07V-097 and have the relay replaced. If the engine has stalled on you, get it fixed before driving again.

issues.t: Rear tires wear out very quickly
issues.sym: Rear tires that wear down or cup far earlier than expected, sometimes with a humming noise from the rear.
issues.why: The rear wheels can toe inward too much when the car is loaded, partly from bump stops that deform. Acura issued service bulletins with new bump stops and a revised alignment.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether service bulletin 05-050 / 05-076 was done on your car, and have a shop check the rear alignment before buying new tires.

issues.t: Cracked dashboard
issues.sym: Cracks spreading across the top of the dashboard, sometimes with creaks or rattles.
issues.why: The dashboard material on this generation tends to split with age and sun exposure.
issues.next: Mostly cosmetic. A dash cover and sunshade slow it down. Have a shop confirm that cracks near the passenger air bag door are not affecting it.

issues.t: Torque converter shudder
issues.sym: A shudder or vibration, like driving over rumble strips, felt at roughly city and suburban speeds.
issues.why: The lock-up clutch inside the torque converter can grab unevenly. Acura released a software update and extended torque converter coverage for these cars.
issues.next: Ask an Acura dealer about service bulletins 16-033 and 16-036, which cover a software update and torque converter replacement for a limited time and mileage.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: Oil level dropping fast between changes, a low oil pressure light, and in bad cases misfires or blue smoke.
issues.why: The oil control rings on the pistons can clog with carbon, letting oil get burned in the cylinders. Acura extended warranty coverage on these engines and repairs involve new pistons and rings.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and top up as needed. Ask a dealer about bulletin B18-009 / B19-006 and the warranty extension, and keep records of oil added.

issues.t: Jerky low-speed shifting in the dual-clutch
issues.sym: Hesitation pulling away from a stop, jerks between low gears, or rough shifting in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: Many owners of early TLX four-cylinder cars reported rough low-speed behavior from the dual-clutch transmission, and Acura released software updates to improve it.
issues.next: Have a dealer check for and install the latest transmission software. If shifting stays rough, have the transmission inspected.

issues.t: Transmission may not go into Park
issues.sym: The shifter will not engage Park, or the car is not held firmly in Park.
issues.why: A contaminated parking pawl or a loose or broken park rod inside the nine-speed automatic can stop it from locking into Park.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 14V-779. Use the parking brake every time you park until the dealer has inspected or replaced the transmission.

issues.t: Transmission can shift into neutral on its own
issues.sym: Sudden loss of drive power while driving, as if the car slipped into neutral.
issues.why: Weak wire crimps in the transmission wiring can send a false signal that drops the transmission into neutral.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 16V-640 and have the transmission software updated.

issues.t: Fuel pump loses output
issues.sym: Hesitation on acceleration, hard starting, or the engine stalling.
issues.why: Fine particles in the fuel can clog the fuel pump and reduce how much fuel it delivers.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 19V-060, which updates software and replaces the pump if needed.

issues.t: Connecting rod bearing can wear and seize
issues.sym: A knocking noise from the engine, rough running, a check engine light, or the engine stalling and not restarting.
issues.why: A manufacturing error can leave a connecting rod bearing prone to wearing out and seizing, which damages the engine.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 23V-751. Stop driving if the engine starts knocking and have the dealer inspect it.

issues.t: Timing belt teeth can separate
issues.sym: Rough running, the engine stalling, or the engine not restarting.
issues.why: Teeth on the timing belt can come apart, throwing off valve timing.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 19V-298. Dealers replace the belt and repair any resulting engine damage.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and stall the engine
issues.sym: Engine sputtering, running rough, a check engine light, or stalling while driving and not restarting.
issues.why: The low-pressure fuel pump inside the tank has a plastic impeller that can swell and stick, so the pump stops delivering fuel.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for open recalls 21V-215 (2019-2020) and 23V-858, which expanded the fix to earlier TLX years, and have the pump replaced for free. A stall at speed is dangerous, so do not put it off.

issues.t: Passenger seat weight sensor can crack (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger air bag status light acting oddly, or an air bag warning light.
issues.why: The front passenger seat weight sensor can crack and short circuit, so the air bag may go off when it should be switched off or fail to switch off for a child.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recalls. Recall 24V-064 covers 2020-2021 TLX; the later recall 26V-332 covers 2018-2021 TLX and also some 2023 cars. Keep children in the back seat until the sensor is replaced.

issues.t: Brake pedal pivot pin may not be secured
issues.sym: The brake pedal feels loose, sits in an odd position, or moves sideways.
issues.why: The pin the brake pedal pivots on may not have been properly secured, so the pedal can shift out of position.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open recall 25V-391 and have the pedal inspected. Get it checked right away if the pedal feels loose.

issues.t: Type S engine can stall or lose power
issues.sym: Sudden loss of power or the engine stalling while driving.
issues.why: A software error in the fuel injection control unit can cut power or stall the engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the VIN for open recall 25V-031 and have the free reprogramming done.

issues.t: Power steering assist can cut out from a software fault
issues.sym: The steering suddenly turns heavy, usually with a power steering warning on the dash.
issues.why: A software error can push the electric power steering into a protective backup mode that switches off the assist. Acura recalled the cars to reprogram the steering control unit.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check your VIN for this recall and book the free software update. If the steering goes heavy, slow down, pull over when safe and have the car checked before driving on.

issues.t: Fuel tank filler neck weld can leak
issues.sym: A gasoline smell around the rear of the car, fuel drips, or a check engine light for an evaporative leak.
issues.why: The joint between the fuel filler neck and the tank may not have been welded properly at the factory, so fuel or vapor can escape. Acura recalled the cars to replace the fuel tank assembly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall. If you smell fuel or see a leak, park outside away from anything that could ignite it and have the car towed to a dealer.

issues.t: Front suspension clunk in hot weather
issues.sym: A clunk from the front of the car over bumps or when pulling away, mostly on hot days.
issues.why: Acura issued a service bulletin for a front suspension clunk that shows up in warm temperatures on these cars.
issues.next: Mention Acura bulletin 12-041 to a dealer or shop. It is an annoyance more than a danger, but have any new front-end noise looked at to rule out worn parts.

issues.t: Clicking or ticking from the rear seat, wheel well or moonroof area
issues.sym: Light clicking, tapping or ticking sounds from behind the rear seat, near a rear wheel well, or around the upper door pillar and moonroof.
issues.why: Interior trim and body panels can rub or tap against each other. Acura published separate bulletins for each noise location.
issues.next: No rush. Ask a dealer or body shop about Acura bulletins 11-024, 11-025 and 11-027 the next time the car is in.

issues.t: Power window reverses on its own or moves slowly
issues.sym: A window goes up and then drops back down by itself, moves slowly, or makes noise while moving.
issues.why: The window can bind in its run channel, which trips the pinch protection and sends it back down. Acura issued a bulletin for these two model years.
issues.next: Have the window channels checked and ask about Acura bulletin 10-014. Until then, hold the switch to close the window fully before leaving the car.

issues.t: Worn ignition switch can stall the engine
issues.sym: The engine cuts out while driving or will not start, and the dash lights may flicker when the key is moved.
issues.why: The contacts inside the ignition switch wear and lose their grip on the circuit that keeps the engine running.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Have the switch replaced under the recall; an engine that quits in traffic takes the power steering and brake assist with it.

issues.t: Key can be taken out without the car in Park
issues.sym: The key pulls out of the ignition with the shifter still in Drive or Neutral, and the car can creep once nobody is holding the brake.
issues.why: The interlock that is meant to trap the key until the shifter reaches Park wears and stops doing its job.
issues.next: Have the interlock and switch replaced under the recall, and set the parking brake every time until it is fixed; the car can roll away.

issues.t: Passenger air bag may not inflate correctly (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing shows in normal driving; the fault only matters in a crash.
issues.why: A part inside the passenger air bag inflator was welded badly, so the bag may not open the way it should.
issues.next: Have the air bag module replaced under the recall; nobody can tell from the seat whether their bag is one of the bad ones.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckles may not hold in a crash
issues.sym: The buckle may feel normal, or it may release more easily than it should when knocked.
issues.why: Some front buckles were built out of spec, and some cars were repaired with buckles that do not meet the standard.
issues.next: Have the buckles checked and replaced under the recall; a belt that lets go in a crash leaves the occupant unprotected.

issues.t: Front air bag sensor bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Nothing in normal driving, and usually no air bag warning light either.
issues.why: The bolts holding a front impact sensor were not tightened enough, so the sensor may not read a crash properly.
issues.next: Have the sensor mounting checked under the recall; loose sensors can delay or prevent the front air bags from firing.

issues.t: Some replacement accelerator pedals can stick
issues.sym: The pedal feels sticky or stays down, and the engine does not drop back to idle when the foot comes off.
issues.why: Certain aftermarket pedal assemblies sold for these cars can bind in their housing.
issues.next: Stop driving and have the pedal identified and replaced if one of the recalled parts was fitted; a throttle that will not close is dangerous.

issues.t: A replacement front lower ball joint can separate
issues.sym: Clunking or knocking from a front corner, loose or wandering steering, and in the worst case the front wheel folds under.
issues.why: A ball joint sold for these cars can be fitted where it does not belong and then pulls apart in service.
issues.next: If the front ball joints have been replaced with aftermarket parts, have them identified and changed under the recall; a joint that separates collapses the suspension.

issues.t: Takata driver air bag inflator can rupture (recall)
issues.sym: No warning signs. The danger only shows up if the driver air bag goes off in a crash.
issues.why: The driver air bag inflator in these TLs can let in moisture over the years and burst when it deploys, throwing metal pieces into the cabin. Some replacement inflators fitted under earlier recalls were also recalled.
issues.next: Check the VIN for open air bag recalls right away and book the free inflator replacement at an Acura dealer, even if an earlier air bag recall was already done.

issues.t: Electric power steering can suddenly fail
issues.sym: A power steering or EPS warning on the dash, then the steering wheel suddenly becomes very heavy or stiff, sometimes while turning or at highway speed. It may come and go.
issues.why: Owners and dealers trace most cases to a failed electric power steering control module, and some cars also needed sensors or the steering rack.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. If the warning comes on, slow down, grip the wheel firmly and pull over when safe. Have the steering system codes read before driving far, and ask the dealer whether any recall, bulletin or goodwill coverage applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Cracked exhaust manifold
issues.sym: A ticking or loud exhaust noise from under the hood, worst on cold starts, sometimes with an exhaust smell in the cabin or a check engine light.
issues.why: The exhaust manifold on the 5-cylinder engine is prone to cracking from repeated heating and cooling. Owners report Honda covered the part on some earlier cars, but not on many 1998s.
issues.next: If you smell exhaust inside, drive with windows cracked and get it inspected soon, because exhaust fumes in the cabin are dangerous. A shop can confirm the crack and replace the manifold.

issues.t: 9-speed automatic jerks between gears
issues.sym: Rough or jerky shifts at low speed, the car lurching when slowing to a stop, slamming into gear when cold, or hesitation when you press the gas.
issues.why: The nine-speed automatic used with the V6 shifted poorly in many early cars. Dealers mostly applied software updates, and Acura issued bulletins on transmission software and on the correct fluid level, since too much or too little fluid can cause hard shifts or slipping.
issues.next: Ask an Acura dealer to check for and install the latest transmission software. If shifting stays harsh or the car hesitates in traffic, have the transmission inspected while it is still under any coverage.

issues.t: Engine won't restart after auto idle stop
issues.sym: After the engine shuts off at a stop light, it does not restart when you lift off the brake. Warning lights come on and the dash may say to press the brake and push start. It is more common in cold weather and with an older battery.
issues.why: The idle-stop restart can fail because of high cylinder pressure or low cranking power, and a weak battery makes it worse. Acura issued bulletins, a software update and a warranty extension covering the starter and idle-stop restart on 2015-2020 TLX models.
issues.next: Ask an Acura dealer to check your VIN for the idle-stop software update and extended coverage, and have the battery tested. You can switch off auto idle stop with its button until it is fixed.

issues.t: Check engine light for misfire or lean running
issues.sym: A check engine light, sometimes flashing, with rough idle or a stumble. Codes point to misfires or a lean fuel mixture.
issues.why: Acura sent dealers a series of messages about misfire and fuel-trim codes on 2016-2020 V6 models, including the TLX.
issues.next: Have the codes read and ask the dealer to check for any updates or bulletins that apply to your VIN. Do not drive hard with a flashing check engine light.

issues.t: Check engine light from a sticking purge valve
issues.sym: A check engine light with an evaporative-system code (often P0441). The car usually drives normally.
issues.why: The purge control valve that lets fuel vapor into the engine can stick. Acura issued a bulletin for the purge valve and dealer messages for 2018-2020 V6 TLX models.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight, then have the code read. Replacing the purge valve is a simple repair.

issues.t: Oil leak from the valve cover gasket
issues.sym: Oil seeping from the top of the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, or oily residue around the spark plug area.
issues.why: Acura sent dealers a series of messages investigating valve cover (head cover) gasket oil leaks on 2020-2021 four-cylinder TLX models.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the gasket replaced. Check the oil level often until it is fixed.

issues.t: Factory tires may lose air suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: A tire loses air quickly, with a tire pressure warning, a pull to one side or vibration.
issues.why: Some tires fitted at the factory may be damaged, so they can lose pressure suddenly. Honda recalled the affected cars to inspect and replace those tires.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the tires inspected. Watch for tire pressure warnings until it is done.
